title: Zostel enters premium hospitality with Zo Selections
summary:
Hospitality brand Zostel has launched Zo Selections, a premium hospitality vertical under its parent company Zo World, with its first property opening in Jaipur. The property offers private rooms, jacuzzi suites, common spaces and workstations.
Founded in 2013, Zostel has grown from a 24-bed hostel in Jodhpur to a network of around 5,000 beds across India, Nepal and Thailand. The company said it has recorded more than 5 million journeys across its properties.
Zo Selections targets travellers who have moved beyond hostel dorms but continue to seek social experiences during their stays. The Jaipur property features bonfires, workshops, sundowners and an in-house restaurant, Amaano, which serves Rajasthani cuisine.
The new vertical expands Zostel’s hospitality portfolio, which includes Zostel Plus, Zostel Homes and Zo House. The company plans to open its next Zo Selections property in Gokarna, followed by locations in Mussoorie, Pench and Lonavla.
The launch comes as Zo World expands its hospitality network. Zostel recently opened its 100th property and its first overseas location in Phuket, while the group has also expanded into Europe through Safestay. Zo World is targeting 10,000 beds as it enters the premium hospitality segment.

title: Oppex AI raises Rs 4.2 Cr in pre-seed round led by Info Edge Ventures
summary:
Oppex AI, an AI-native platform for production operations, has raised Rs 4.2 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Info Edge Ventures.
The fresh funds will be utilised to accelerate product development, expand the team, and scale deployments with customers, Oppex AI said in a press release.
Launched in June last year by Prasun Kumar and Pranit Kumar, Oppex AI builds an AI-native platform for production operations, with the aim of transforming incident management from human-led to AI-led. Its agentic platform brings together context from observability, customer support, cloud infrastructure, internal runbooks, and other enterprise systems to understand production incidents and automate incident response.
Oppex AI addresses the growing production bottleneck by building an AI-powered system designed specifically for production operations. The startup aims to automate and streamline the detection, investigation, and resolution of production incidents, helping engineering teams spend less time firefighting and more time building products.
By creating an AI layer for production, the company seeks to ensure that faster software development does not come at the cost of reliability, customer experience, or trust. This would enable organisations to fully realise the benefits of AI-driven software development.
The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform is being adopted by enterprise customers across India, the UK, the EU, and the US. It plans to strengthen its agentic platform and expand its capabilities as it works towards making AI-led production operations a reality for enterprise technology teams.
As AI accelerates software development and increases deployment velocity, production environments are becoming more complex. This is creating demand for agentic systems that can unify signals from logs, metrics, infrastructure, applications, and internal knowledge bases to identify root causes and recommend or execute remediation.

title: Exclusive: Qualcomm Ventures to lead $60 Mn round for Ultrahuman
summary:
Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman is raising Rs 583 crore (around $60 million) in its Series C round led by Qualcomm Ventures and with the participation of Alpha Wave, Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings, Deepinder Goyal, Blume Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Steadview Capital, GGM Family Trust, Krypton Fund, and others.
The board at Ultrahuman has passed a special resolution to issue 3,623 Series C and 3832 Series C1 compulsorily convertible preference shares at an issue price of Rs 7,79,500 and Rs 7,85,300, respectively, to raise Rs 583 crore (approximately $60 million), according to its regulatory filings sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Qualcomm Ventures will lead the round with an investment of Rs 143 crore, followed by Alpha Wave, which will invest Rs 114 crore. Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings will put in Rs 95 crore, while Blume Ventures will invest Rs 90 crore.
Deepinder Goyal will invest Rs 47.4 crore, while Nexus Venture Partners and Krypton Fund will contribute Rs 18.9 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively. The remaining amount will be invested by GGM Family Trust, Steadview Capital, InCred Wealth, Joy Bhakat and other investors.
According to Entrackr’s estimates, the funding round values the company at around $363 million post-money, marking a 65% jump from its previous Series B valuation.
As per the filing, the company plans to use the fresh proceeds for growth, expansion, and other general corporate purposes.
A July ET report also said that Ultrahuman is in talks to raise $60 million.
It’s worth noting that Ultrahuman’s co-founders, Mohit Kumar and Vatsal Singhal, had earlier sold their first startup, Runnr, to Zomato in September 2017. Zomato later leveraged Runnr, which was merged with Mumbai-based TinyOwl, to strengthen its in-house delivery fleet.
Ultrahuman operates a self-quantification platform and offers products such as the Ring Air smart ring, the M1 Live glucose monitoring wearable, and the Blood Vision blood testing platform, among others. Prior to this round, the company had raised more than $60 million, including a $35 million Series B round and a $17.5 million Series A round in October 2022.
Ultrahuman reported Rs 565 crore in revenue and Rs 73 crore profit after tax in FY25, while it has projected Rs 1,000 crore in revenue for FY26.

title: Rainmatter leads Rs 30 Cr pre-Series A round in Minimac Systems
summary:
Industrial deep-tech company Minimac Systems has raised Rs 30 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Rainmatter, the investment firm backed by Zerodha, with participation from other venture capital firms.
The proceeds will be used to advance R&D in miniaturised treatment infrastructure, fleet automation and fluid analytics. The company will also scale its Recycling on Wheels model through regional hubs across major industrial clusters and strengthen its commercial, digital and operational capabilities, Minimac Systems said in a press release.
Founded in 2012 by Anshuman Agrawal, Minimac Systems focuses on lubricant lifecycle management, reliability and circularity. The company develops miniaturised fluid-treatment systems, operates Recycling on Wheels, a mobile on-site lubricant restoration model, and is developing Lubricants as a Service.
India is the world's third-largest lubricant market, consuming more than 5 million tonnes of lubricants and greases annually, while its annual base-oil import bill has crossed $2.7 billion, according to market research cited by the company.
Minimac's platform covers three stages of lubricant management. NanoCircularity monitors lubricant inside machines through condition monitoring, contamination control and fluid-health analytics. MicroCircularity restores recoverable lubricant at industrial plants by removing contaminants, moisture and degradation by-products. MacroCircularity sends lubricant that cannot be restored to registered re-refiners for conversion into re-refined base oil (RRBO).
Its Recycling on Wheels model uses mobile, miniaturised treatment systems with processing capacities ranging from around 10 to 4,000 litres per minute. These systems assess and treat lubricant at industrial sites before returning it to service. The company aims to abate 860 gigagrams of CO₂e emissions by 2034.
Minimac plans to manage the lubricant lifecycle within industrial plants, covering supply, monitoring, restoration, compliance and end-of-life recovery. Its proposed contracts will be based on uptime, fluid health and agreed outcomes rather than product sales alone.
The company claims to have deployed more than 2,500 miniaturised fluid-treatment systems with a combined installed processing capacity of over 300,000 litres per minute. It has worked across more than 2,200 industrial assets and kept over 14 million litres of lubricant in productive use across India and international markets. Its customers include NTPC, Adani Power, JSW Steel and Tata Steel.
The lubricant circularity segment is still niche in India, with startups such as Santosh Petrochemical Innovations and ReVivo's LubeLoop working on used-oil re-refining and resource recovery.
In March 2026, Re Sustainability partnered with Indian Oil Corporation to build a nationwide used-oil collection and recycling ecosystem, with plans to collect 100 KTA of used lubricants and set up a 50–100 KTA re-refining facility.
Adjacent industrial circularity startups are also attracting investor interest. In January 2026, PolyCycl raised a Series A round from Rainmatter for its chemical recycling technology.

As of 2:30 PM today, Eternal’s shares were trading at Rs 325.5 apiece, valuing the company at a market capitalization of Rs 3,13,299 crore, or nearly $33 billion.

title: Unacademy closes UpGrad deal at $200 Mn
summary:
Edtech major Unacademy has closed its acquisition by UpGrad for just over $200 million, marking a 94% decline from its peak valuation of around $3.4 billion in 2021. 
Unacademy co-founder and CEO Gaurav Munjal confirmed the completion of the deal in a post on Tuesday, acknowledging that the company had raised money at its peak but was now being sold at a fraction of that valuation. 
Entrackr had exclusively reported earlier that UpGrad was set to close the acquisition of Unacademy in a deal valued at around Rs 1,955 crore. The transaction was structured as an all-stock deal, with Munjal expected to continue leading Unacademy following the combination.
Interestingly, Munjal said the deal was not driven by a cash crunch. According to him, Unacademy currently has a topline of around Rs 400 crore, with most of its businesses either profitable or near profitable. The company also has around Rs 900 crore in the bank, he added.
According to Munjal, Unacademy had the option to continue independently but chose to combine with UpGrad after discussions with Screwvala and a belief that the merger would create a stronger education ecosystem.
The acquisition gives UpGrad an entry into the online test-preparation segment, including categories such as UPSC, JEE, NEET and GATE. It also adds Unacademy’s educator network and other businesses to UpGrad’s existing higher education, upskilling and study-abroad portfolio.
Munjal also highlighted Unacademy’s broader impact, saying its educators have crossed 10 billion views on YouTube. He added that the company conducted four ESOP buybacks that created liquidity for employees.
While the exit value is far below Unacademy’s peak valuation, Munjal said he remains confident that shareholders can create significant value from the combined business going forward.

title: Deep-tech aerospace startup Alteon raises $2.5 Mn led by Lachy Groom
summary:
Deep-tech aerospace startup Alteon has raised $2.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Lachy Groom, with participation from Together Fund.
The round follows a recent flight test in which Alteon’s aircraft demonstrated autonomous flight within a metre of the ocean’s surface. The test helped derisk a key component of the manoeuvre on which the company’s autonomous, high-endurance flight capability relies.
The fresh capital will be used for offshore tests aimed at achieving autonomous dynamic soaring without propulsion. Alteon will also scale its R&D efforts to deploy a fleet of such aircraft over the ocean, the company said in a press release.
Founded in 2025 by Samay Sanghvi, Alteon develops autonomous aircraft designed to fly for months by using dynamic soaring to harvest energy from the atmosphere. The Bengaluru-based startup is building a new class of ultra-high-endurance aircraft that can remain airborne by drawing energy from the environment.
Its autonomous dynamic-soaring vehicles extract energy from wind gradients, similar to albatrosses, to remain airborne for extended periods. A key engineering challenge is enabling the aircraft to perform this manoeuvre autonomously close to the surface of a moving ocean.
Alteon plans to progressively test its ability to harvest energy from wind until the aircraft can sustain flight without propulsion, similar to an albatross.
The company’s aircraft fleets can carry payloads for applications such as mapping weather and ocean conditions, tracking ships and fishing activity, monitoring critical infrastructure, and supporting defence, search and rescue, scientific and industrial operations.
Alteon said its fleets could provide a continuous, real-time layer of capabilities over the ocean at a fraction of the cost of ships, satellites and large offshore installations.
The funding comes as India’s autonomous aircraft ecosystem gains investor interest. Airbound recently raised $37 million in a Series A round to develop lightweight autonomous delivery aircraft.
While dynamic-soaring aviation remains an early and highly specialised segment, recent funding activity points to growing interest in autonomous flight, advanced drones and next-generation aerospace technologies in India.

The shares were traded at Rs 630 each, while global and domestic institutions including Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, ICICI Prudential and SBI Mutual Fund were among the buyers.

Other early investors have also pared their holdings. ADIA sold around Rs 1,960 crore worth of shares in June, while Temasek offloaded around Rs 1,940 crore in July. Together with SoftBank's two transactions, these sales amounted to around Rs 9,660 crore between June and August.

title: Niyo to acquire Capital India Finance’s RemitX forex business
summary:
Bengaluru-based travel-fintech platform Niyo has signed an agreement to acquire the forex and cross-border business of Capital India Finance, which operates under the RemitX brand. 
The deal will bring RemitX’s branch network, distribution partners, employees and brand under Niyo.
RemitX operates 32 branches across 16 states and more than 30 cities, including Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets. The acquisition will take Niyo’s physical presence to more than 40 locations across India. It will also add over 2,500 distribution partners across travel, overseas education and corporate segments.
More than 200 RemitX employees, including its leadership team, are expected to join Niyo’s wholly owned subsidiary Kanji Forex. 
The combined business will offer foreign currency, forex cards and outward remittance services through both physical branches and Niyo’s digital platform.
Niyo entered the regulated forex business in 2024 through its acquisition of Kanji Forex, which holds an Authorised Dealer Category-II licence. In August 2026, the Reserve Bank of India granted Kanji Forex a perpetual AD-II licence with an expanded scope covering additional remittance services.
The acquisition will help Niyo expand its forex distribution network beyond major cities and increase its presence in the cross-border payments market. The company had earlier planned to build a network of 50 branches over the next two to three years.

title: Indian startup funding nears $1 Bn in August after July slowdown
summary:
August saw a couple of $100 million-plus deals, including River Mobility and Navi, pushing India’s startup funding closer to the $1 billion mark. Notably, early-stage deals accounted for around 42% of the month’s funding, led by rounds in Airbound, Centricity, and InRisk Labs. Despite mixed market sentiment around startup IPOs, Shiprocket, Milky Mist, and Leap made strong market debuts at a premium. The month also saw a couple of layoffs, while one startup shut down operations.
[Funding overview]

According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $954 million across 88 deals in August. The total included 13 growth and late-stage deals worth $555 million and 75 early-stage deals worth $400 million. Of the 88 deals, eight were disclosed without funding amounts during the month.
[M-o-M and Y-o-Y trend]

Month-on-month, startup funding jumped 44.3% to $955 million in August from $662 million in July, making it the third-highest monthly total of 2026. Year-on-year, funding remained largely stable at $955 million in August 2026 versus $961 million in August 2025, while the number of deals declined from 100 to 88.
[Top 10 growth/late stage deals]
Growth and late-stage funding in August was led by EV startup River Mobility, which raised $120 million in a Series C round. Navi and Yulu followed with $100 million and $93 million, respectively, while AI startup Sarvam AI secured $74 million. Other notable deals included Third Wave Coffee, Leap India, Matter, BlissClub, Matel, and BGauss, with investments spread across mobility, fintech, AI, F&B, supply chain, EV, e-commerce, and manufacturing.

[Top 10 early stage deals]
Early-stage funding in August was led by aviation startup Airbound, which raised $37 million, followed by wealthtech platform Centricity with $30 million and fintech startup InRisk Labs with $27 million. Other notable deals included CtrlS, Runable, Nexedge Capital, NeoGeo, Rezolv, InstaAstro, and HomeRun, with investments spread across aviation, fintech, data centres, AI, deeptech, spiritual tech, and quick commerce.

[Mergers and Acquisitions]
Mergers and acquisitions remained active in August, with deals spread across healthtech, fintech, edtech, AI and spacetech. Temple acquired London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous, while Healthify merged with Berry Street. Other deals included GalaxEye’s acquisition of StarOps, Imarticus Learning’s acquisition of BELLS Institute, Mintoak’s acquisition of ICC Loyalty and ET Now’s acquisition of OpiGo.

[City and segment wise deals]
Bengaluru continued to dominate startup funding in August, accounting for 47 deals worth $657.65 million, or nearly 69% of the total funding. Delhi-NCR followed with $127.92 million across 20 deals, while Mumbai secured $83.35 million across eight deals. Hyderabad and Pune accounted for a smaller share, with $27.5 million and $22.6 million, respectively.
EV led startup funding in August with $256.14 million across six deals, making up 26.9% of the total funding. Fintech followed with $200.9 million across eight deals, while AI secured $134.4 million across 13 deals. E-commerce raised $48.23 million across 12 deals, followed by deeptech with $40.3 million.
[Stage wise deals]
Series A deals led the funding activity with $313.44 million across 27 deals in August, which made up 32.85% of the total funding. Seed-stage startups raised $46.43 million across 25 deals, while Series B deals secured $141.3 million across five deals. Pre-Series A and pre-seed rounds raised $26.4 million and $4.05 million, respectively.

[Layoffs, shutdowns, departures and key hirings]
August saw 620 layoffs, including 350 employees at Even Healthcare and 270 at listed company Zomato (now Eternal). Meanwhile, e-grocery startup Satvacart announced its shutdown. On the leadership front, startups recorded 31 key executive hires and three senior-level departures.
[Trends]
Early-stage funding remains strong: Early-stage deals contributed $400 million, or nearly 42% of total funding. Airbound, Centricity and InRisk Labs led the segment with sizeable rounds.
Aviation and spacetech gain momentum:  Aviation and spacetech attracted strong investor interest in August, led by aviation startup Airbound, which raised $37 million, and spacetech startup Inspecity, which secured $10.5 million. July also saw back-to-back deals across these sectors, which highlights continued investor interest in aviation and spacetech.
Flipkart Minutes overtakes Swiggy Instamart in dark stores: Flipkart Minutes had 627 dark stores across India’s top 10 cities in August, surpassing Swiggy Instamart’s 615, as Flipkart continued to expand its quick-commerce network.
Navi’s $100 Mn round strengthens IPO prospects: Navi’s first institutional funding round of $100 million signals stronger investor confidence in the fintech and creates a more favourable environment for the company as it moves towards a potential IPO.
EV emerges as the top-funded segment: EV startups led funding in August, raising $256.14 million across six deals, which accounted for 26.9% of the total funding.
[Conclusion]
August reflected a stronger recovery in India’s startup ecosystem after the July slowdown, with investor interest spread across EV, AI, aviation, spacetech and early-stage ventures. The month also brought notable shifts in quick commerce and positive signals from IPO-bound startups, while large growth-stage rounds showed that investors continue to back companies with clear scale-up potential. Overall, the funding activity points to a more active market, with capital flowing into both established startups and emerging sectors.

title: Battery-swapping startup Yuma Energy raises $35 Mn from Magna International
summary:
Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) provider Yuma Energy has raised $35 million in a Series A funding round led by Magna International Inc.
The Bengaluru-based startup has also acquired battery technology company Grinntech to strengthen its battery technology and manufacturing capabilities.
The fresh funds will be used to expand Yuma Energy’s battery-swapping infrastructure across India and broaden its customer base across EV users, fleet operators and OEM partners, the company said in a press release.
Founded in 2023, Yuma Energy operates a battery-swapping network for electric mobility. The company claims to have delivered more than 60 million battery swaps through a network of over 100,000 batteries, 2,500+ charging units and more than 400 touch points across 18 cities.
Yuma Energy powers Yulu’s electric fleet and also provides open-access battery-swapping services to third-party original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and last-mile delivery operators.
The company plans to further expand its infrastructure and technology platform to serve riders, fleet operators and OEM partners and support the wider adoption of electric mobility.
BaaS providers separate the cost of the battery from the vehicle, allowing users to access charged batteries through subscription or pay-per-use models. The model can lower the upfront cost of EVs and reduce downtime through battery swapping.
Other startups such as Battery Smart, Sun Mobility and Gogoro are also building battery-swapping and energy infrastructure networks in India. Battery Smart raised around Rs 124 crore ($13 million) in debt from responsAbility Investments AG in July to expand its swapping network.

title: InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy officially announce merger
summary:
Gurugram-based insurtech startups InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy have officially announced their merger to create a unified insurance distribution platform with a pan-India presence.
The combined entity will operate under the InsuranceDekho brand, with InsuranceDekho founder and CEO Ankit Agrawal leading the business. The merger brings together InsuranceDekho’s presence across northern and western India with RenewBuy’s network in southern markets.
The platform will offer motor, health, life and commercial insurance products from multiple insurers. It plans to integrate the technology platforms of both companies and deploy AI across partner onboarding, product recommendations and insurance advisory. The company will also provide digital tools for policy issuance and customer service.
The merged entity generated more than Rs 6,600 crore in insurance premiums through its POSP network in FY26. It has over 6 lakh digital partners and reaches 98.57% of India’s pin codes. Together, the companies have facilitated more than 2 crore insurance policies since inception.
InsuranceDekho is also preparing to file its DRHP by the end of September, with plans to launch an IPO by March 2027. The company is targeting a Rs 2,500-3,000 crore issue at an estimated valuation of around Rs 9,500 crore. 
The founders of both companies will continue with the merged entity, while teams across technology, distribution, product and operations will be integrated. The company said it will work with IRDAI and other stakeholders to expand insurance access across Tier-2, Tier-3 and smaller markets.
The merger talks began in October 2024. InsuranceDekho received a composite insurance broking licence from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in July 2024.
InsuranceDekho last raised $70 million in a round co-led by Beams Fintech Fund and Japan’s Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) in March 2025. Meanwhile, RenewBuy raised $40 million from Japanese insurance major Dai-ichi Life Holdings in July 2023.

summary:
Space infrastructure and mission operations company Kepler Aerospace has raised $8 million in a seed funding round led by Blue Ashva Capital, with participation from Finvolve India Accelerator and other investors.
The proceeds will be used to develop and deploy next-generation space-based persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities, while scaling its mission operations and avionics-as-a-service businesses, Kepler Aerospace said in a press release.
Founded in July 2018 by Navneet Singh and Kiran Sharma, Kepler Aerospace builds scalable space and ground systems for strategic, defence and commercial missions. Its capabilities span satellite avionics and subsystems, ground infrastructure, mission operations and space-based intelligence.
The Bengaluru-based startup said its technology is designed around reliability, automation, security and scalability, enabling satellite operators and mission stakeholders to deploy and manage increasingly complex space missions. The company caters to strategic, defence and commercial applications.
Kepler Aerospace aims to address the growing demand for persistent, low-latency intelligence from space. It seeks to reduce intelligence latency from months to minutes through persistent ISR systems and integrated mission infrastructure.
The company claims to have secured two IDEX prime contracts to provide swarming ISR constellations to India’s defence space ecosystem, supported by around $4 million in grants under the IDEX programme.
Through a network of more than 70 ground stations, Kepler provides satellite communication, tracking, telemetry, command and mission operations capabilities for a growing range of space missions.
The segment is gaining momentum as India’s private space ecosystem matures, with around 440 space-tech startups registered in the country as of August 2026.
In the space-tech segment, Digantara, a space surveillance and intelligence company, raised $50 million in a Series B round to expand its space-based surveillance capabilities, manufacturing infrastructure and global operations. title: UPI hits new record with 24.51 Bn transactions in August
summary:
Unified Payments Interface (UPI) posted its highest ever monthly transaction volume in August 2026, with 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The August numbers surpassed July’s 23.66 billion transactions. However, transaction value declined marginally from Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July.
On a daily basis, UPI processed 791 million transactions, while the average daily transaction value stood at Rs 96,205 crore.
Compared to July, transaction volume increased 3.6% from 23.66 billion, while transaction value declined 0.2% from Rs 29.88 lakh crore. On a year-on-year basis, transaction volume grew 22%, while transaction value increased 20%.
UPI crossed the 23 billion monthly transaction mark for the first time in May and has continued to see strong growth in subsequent months.
As of July, Walmart-backed digital payments platform PhonePe retained its lead in the UPI ecosystem with 10.86 billion transactions, followed by Google Pay with 7.65 billion and Paytm with 1.90 billion transactions. PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm accounted for 45.89%, 32.33% and 8.05% of UPI transaction volume, respectively. NPCI is yet to release the app-wise transaction data for August.
In August, discussions around the merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI resurfaced after the government proposed changes to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The amendment gives the government flexibility to decide which electronic payment modes remain exempt from merchant charges. The government has clarified that consumers will not be charged for UPI transactions, while any future MDR would apply only to a limited set of merchant transactions.
Recently, the Maldives launched a real-time payment corridor with India, further expanding UPI’s global footprint. UPI merchant payments are now live in 10 international markets: Bhutan, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Qatar, Cambodia and the Maldives. Greece remains connected for person-to-person transfers, while Singapore and Nepal also support remittance linkages.

title: EquityList launches AI-native cap table and compliance platform
summary:
Equity and shareholder management platform EquityList has launched an AI-native cap table and compliance operating system, aimed at automating equity management and compliance workflows for companies.
EquityList said the platform manages more than $20 billion in securities across more than 650 companies and more than 80,000 stakeholders across 16 countries. Its customer base includes Tata Consumer Products, Swiggy, Angel One, Shiprocket, BlackBuck, BlueStone, Flipkart, Rapido, Slice, Sarvam, Tabby.ai and Salla, among others.
The new platform uses AI to analyse cap tables, legal documents, filings and equity data. It allows finance, HR and compliance teams to query information in plain language and automate routine tasks.
The platform can extract details such as share classes from legal documents, identify compliance gaps and draft equity grants. Each AI-assisted action requires human review and approval before it is reflected in the cap table.
According to EquityList, its AI is built natively into the platform with controls over data access and permitted actions. The company also highlighted its SOC 2 Type II certification, ISO 27001 compliance and alignment with GDPR requirements.
The launch also includes a self-serve onboarding process that uses AI to parse legal documents, cap tables and financial reports. Customers can review and confirm the extracted information instead of entering the data manually.
The company said the underlying cap table data and calculations continue to run on a deterministic engine based on its proprietary data models. AI operates on top of this system to provide analysis and automation.
EquityList plans to expand further into compliance automation and corporate governance workflows, with configurable processes that can run with less manual intervention.
EquityList raised $2.2 million in seed funding in September 2023 from AngelList India, Hustle Fund, Republic, Unpopular Ventures, Mana Ventures, Riverwalk Holdings and Super Capital, with participation from several angel investors.

Hero MotoCorp stood fourth with 18,978 registrations and a 10.37% market share. Its registrations declined 17.45% month on month, while Ola Electric remained fifth with 13,849 registrations and a 7.57% market share.
Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 8,612 registrations and a 4.71% market share. Its registrations dropped 15% month on month. River Mobility and BGauss also saw registrations decline 14.86% and 12.86%, respectively.
Among the smaller players, Motovolt recorded the strongest month-on-month growth, with registrations more than doubled to 1,365 units. Simple Energy remained stable at 1,635 units in August.

title: Exclusive: Wedding services startup Meragi set to raise fresh funds at flat valuation
summary:
Bengaluru-based wedding services startup Meragi is set to raise Rs 28.68 crore in a fresh funding round from its existing investors Accel India, Peak XV Partners, and new investor DG Daiwa Ventures. The round appears to be a bridge round, as the company has not raised any capital in the past two years.

In July 2024, the company had raised $9.1 million in a funding round led by Accel, along with Peak XV Partners and Venture Highway.
The company’s board has passed a special resolution to issue 3,330 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) and 10 equity shares at a price of Rs 85,880.21 per share to raise the fresh capital.
Accel India will lead the round with Rs 14.34 crore, while DG Daiwa Ventures will invest Rs 9.56 crore and Peak XV Partners Rs 5.56 crore.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, Meragi will be valued at around Rs 305 crore post-money, remaining flat compared with its previous funding round.
Founded in 2021 by Mukund Mohan Raj, Abhinav Chandran, and Lakshminarayan B, Meragi provides wedding-related services such as decoration, photography, videography, makeup, hairstyling, mehendi, catering, venues, entertainment, and invitations. 
Following the allotment, Accel India will hold a 22.14% stake in Meragi, followed by Venture Highway and Surge Ventures with 15.92% and 15.85%, respectively. Peak XV Partners and DG Daiwa Ventures will hold 7.80% and 3.17% stakes, respectively.

The company operates in a competitive wedding-services market alongside WedMeGood, ShaadiSaga, Weddingz.in, Shaadilogy, Wedding Cloud, Shaadi Baraati, and The Wedding Brigade.

Groww Asset Management has completed the strategic investment from State Street Investment Management, formally closing a deal first announced in January this year.
The partnership gives State Street a 23% economic interest and 4.85% voting rights in Groww AMC, following the completion of all necessary regulatory approvals. The transaction involved an investment of up to Rs 580 crore through a mix of primary subscription and secondary purchase of shares.
The deal brings together Groww’s asset management business and State Street Investment Management, the asset management arm of US-based financial services giant State Street. State Street had about $5.4 trillion in assets under management as of September 2025.
For Groww, the partnership comes as its AMC business continues to scale. The company had Rs 4,119 crore in assets under management and 1.2 million unique investors as of December 2025, according to Groww’s shareholder letter.  Its AUM had nearly tripled year-on-year to around Rs 4,730 crore by May 2026.
Groww said the partnership will give its AMC access to State Street’s expertise in indexing, ETFs, systematic investing, macroeconomic research and portfolio construction. The collaboration is also expected to support product development, distribution and access to global markets.
The transaction had been awaiting regulatory clearances since the original announcement. The Competition Commission of India (CCI) approved State Street’s acquisition of a stake in Groww AMC in March 2026.

title: PhonePe launches UPI 123Pay for feature phone users without internet
summary:
PhonePe has launched UPI 123Pay, allowing feature phone users across India to make UPI payments without an internet connection.
The service targets India’s 200 million feature phone users and supports key services including person-to-person transfers, merchant payments, balance checks and transaction history.
UPI 123Pay will come pre-installed on select feature phones from Nokia, HMD, Lava and Itel. The service uses an SMS-based system and is designed to work in areas with limited 2G connectivity.
Users can make payments using mobile numbers and UPI IDs, while supported devices will also allow QR code payments.
PhonePe has also introduced an AI-powered voice helpline that supports English and 12 Indian languages, helping users activate and use the service.
The company plans to add features such as bill payments, mobile recharges and Aadhaar-based onboarding in future updates.
The launch comes as PhonePe continues to dominate India’s UPI ecosystem. The Walmart-backed digital payments platform processed nearly 11 billion UPI transactions in July, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
PhonePe accounted for 45.89% of the total UPI transaction volume in July. In value terms, it processed transactions worth Rs 14.44 lakh crore, giving it a 48.33% share of the total UPI transaction value.

title: NPCI set to make UPI AutoPay mandates portable across apps: Report
summary:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) is preparing to make UPI AutoPay mandates portable across apps, a move that could reduce user lock-in and intensify competition among UPI platforms, according to a Mint report.
Under the planned interoperability framework, users will be able to move eligible UPI AutoPay mandates from one UPI app to another without cancelling and recreating them. This could cover recurring payments such as OTT subscriptions, insurance premiums, SIPs, EMIs and utility bills.
For instance, a user with an existing AutoPay mandate on PhonePe could move it to Google Pay or another UPI app, subject to the mandate being eligible. The transfer will be initiated by the user and require authentication through the UPI PIN.
The move could remove one of the lesser-known sources of stickiness for leading UPI apps such as Paytm, PhonePe and Google Pay. Users with multiple recurring payments linked to an app may be less willing to switch if doing so means setting up every mandate again.
With portability, that friction could come down. Smaller UPI apps could potentially attract users from larger platforms without requiring them to rebuild their recurring payment setup.
The development is based on NPCI’s AutoPay enhancement framework issued in 2025, which provided for interoperability of mandates across UPI apps. The feature is now being prepared for implementation and is expected to be highlighted at the upcoming Global Fintech Fest, according to Mint.
The timing is also significant as UPI AutoPay usage has grown sharply. As per the report, the top 10 banks processed nearly 1.8 billion UPI e-mandate transactions in July 2026, more than three times the 585 million transactions recorded in July 2025.
NPCI is also extending portability to the merchant side, allowing businesses to move existing AutoPay mandates between payment service providers.
While the move is unlikely to immediately alter the market shares of leading UPI apps, it removes one layer of user lock-in. In a market dominated by a few large players such as PhonePe and Google Pay, that could give smaller apps more room to compete for users.

summary:
Indoor air-quality company YOGa Clean Air has raised Rs 20 crore in a Series A funding round led by Info Edge Ventures, with participation from Zomato/Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal and Three Words Capital.
The company said in a press release that it will use the fresh capital to deepen its presence in existing markets, expand into new Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities, and extend its systems to public transport and other outdoor environments.
Founded in 2019 by Sachin Panwar, Deepak Raina and Gaurav Nagar, YOGa Clean Air offers its patented Clean Air Bubble technology, which filters incoming air and maintains slightly higher air pressure inside a space to prevent polluted air from entering. The system also manages carbon dioxide levels to maintain indoor air quality.
The Gurugram-based company claims its systems currently serve more than 5,000 families and hundreds of institutions, including hospitals, schools, offices and gyms, across 11 Indian cities, including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. It holds two patents for its technology.
YOGa said its systems have reduced indoor air pollution to single-digit levels even when outdoor pollution crossed 900 µg/m³, while keeping CO₂ levels in check. The company also claims a 100% renewal rate for its annual maintenance contracts.
The indoor air-quality segment has seen startups move beyond conventional air purifiers into areas such as air-quality monitoring, HVAC-integrated filtration, pathogen control, plant-based purification and industrial emission control.
Pune-based NovorbisItus recently secured Rs 13.35 crore ($1.6 million) in seed funding led by Rainmatter for emission-control and air-purification systems. Airth, which develops filters that convert conventional air conditioners into air purifiers, has also raised funding as it expands its indoor air-quality offerings.
Other players in the segment include uBreathe Life, operated by Urban Air Labs, which has received Technology Development Board support for its plant-based indoor air-purification technology, and Biomoneta, which is developing medical-grade air-cleaning solutions.

title: Healthians turns profitable in FY26; revenue jumps 37%
summary:
Following a near-breakeven during FY25, diagnostics and wellness testing platform Healthians turned profitable for the first time in the fiscal year ending March 2026, while continuing to scale its business.
Healthians’ revenue from operations grew 35.7% year-on-year to Rs 357 crore in FY26 from Rs 263 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
The Gurugram-based company offers at-home diagnostic services across more than 250 cities and claims to have conducted over 10 crore tests to date. Diagnostics remained its biggest revenue driver, contributing 99% of the operating revenue, or Rs 353 crore, during the fiscal year. The remaining income came from supplementary and ancillary services.

Healthians also earned Rs 5 crore in interest income, taking its total revenue to Rs 362 crore in FY26 from Rs 270 crore in FY25.
On the cost front, employee benefits remained the company’s largest expense, accounting for 36.8% of its total expenditure. The expense rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 134 crore in FY26. The cost of materials stood at Rs 109 crore, while marketing expenses declined to Rs 44 crore.
Rent, legal, information technology and other overheads pushed Healthians’ total expenditure up 32.4% to Rs 364 crore in FY26 from Rs 275 crore in FY25.
With revenue growing faster than expenses, Healthians turned profitable and posted a net profit of Rs 5.4 crore in FY26, compared with a loss of Rs 4.77 crore in FY25. The company, however, continued to carry accumulated losses of Rs 976 crore.
On a unit economics basis, Healthians spent Rs 1.02 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its EBITDA margin improved to 2.20%, while ROCE stood at -4.86%. At the end of FY26, the company had current assets worth Rs 112.5 crore.
Healthians has raised around $75 million in funding to date, with WestBridge, BEENEXT, DG Ventures and YouWeCan among its key investors. The Bengaluru-based company competes with Orange Health, Redcliffe Labs, Dr Lal PathLabs and other diagnostic players.
The financial turnaround comes amid a leadership transition at Healthians. Founder Deepak Sahni stepped away from all formal executive responsibilities in January 2026 after spending a decade building the company.
While getting close to operating profitability should be welcome, as the numbers show, Healthians has a long way to go yet. Growth from here will hardly be linear, with the high competition in the market and pressure on margins from that. What the competition has achieved is definitely a push for more diagnostics by both institutions and individuals themselves, a trend that would be welcome but for the rising pushback against what many consider ‘unnecessary’ tests. Expanding this market further would need testing solutions that provide a significant indicator of future risks and actions that can be taken in the present. Be it the use of AI or newer approaches to diagnosis beyond the staple blood tests. As a very technology led firm, Healthians will need to see how it can achieve this to manage a real breakthrough in operating metrics.

title: E-grocery startup Satvacart shuts down after 12 years
summary:
Gurugram-based e-grocery startup Satvacart has shut down after 12 years of operations. August 28 was its last day of operations, with the team subsequently disbanded, founder Rahul H. Saxena said in a LinkedIn post.
The shutdown follows several challenging years during which Satvacart explored funding, strategic investment and acquisition opportunities. According to Saxena, the company received capital largely in smaller tranches, which was insufficient to rebuild and scale the business.
“We continued pushing till the very end and explored every realistic funding, strategic investment and acquisition option available to us,” Saxena said.
Satvacart was also in discussions with two larger investors for a significant investment, but neither deal materialised. The startup also held acquisition discussions with multiple players, though none progressed.
Saxena said Satvacart’s profitability-driven approach did not result in the scale that potential investors and acquirers were looking for.
“The past few months had become increasingly difficult,” he said, adding that continuing operations had reached a point where it was coming at the cost of people who had stood by the company.
Founded in 2014, Satvacart was among India’s early online grocery players. It initially started with milk subscriptions in Gurugram before moving to an inventory-led grocery delivery model, operating through micro-clusters and independent warehouses.
In 2015, the startup raised seed funding from Palaash Ventures and angel investors to expand operations, acquire customers and strengthen its technology team.
Unlike many competitors that pursued aggressive customer acquisition and expansion, Satvacart focused on measured growth and profitability. Saxena said the company was among the early online grocery players to demonstrate profitability in the category in 2019.
However, the grocery market has since shifted significantly towards quick commerce, with players such as Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart competing on delivery speed, dark-store density and scale. Ecommerce giants Amazon and Flipkart have also entered the segment with Amazon Now and Flipkart Minutes, respectively.
Satvacart’s smaller scale made it harder to attract larger institutional investors and strategic buyers as competition increasingly shifted towards scale-driven models.
Reflecting on the journey, Saxena said he had no regrets about shutting down the business.
“I genuinely believe I gave Satvacart the very best effort I was capable of,” he said.
After 12 years of building the company across technology, operations, fundraising, marketing, supply chain and customer experience, Saxena concluded: “As this chapter closes, I look forward to the next one.”

summary:
Quick-service burger chain Good Flippin’ Burgers is set to raise fresh funding after a gap of two and a half years, with Delhi-based S.R. Foundation investing Rs 55 crore at a 20% valuation premium.
 
The company’s board passed a special resolution to issue 58,668 Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares at an issue price of Rs 9,374.77 per share to raise fresh capital from S.R. Foundation, according to the company’s regulatory filings with the Registrar of companies.
 
Managed by corporate trustee Rajiv Kumar Gupta, S.R. Foundation operates as a back-end investment vehicle and public charitable trust linked to the DS Group promoter network.
 
In April 2024, the Mumbai-based company had raised Rs 30 crore (approximately $3.6 million) in an extended Series A round from existing investor Tanglin Venture Partners.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation will rise to around Rs 481 crore in the Series B from Rs 400 crore in the extended Series A round, where its valuation surged three-fold.
The seven-year-old firm plans to use the fresh capital for growth, expansion, and general corporate purposes, as per filings.
 
Good Flippin’ Burgers operates a chain of burger restaurants across India. Launched in Mumbai in 2019, the company has 67 outlets across Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai.
 
The QSR chain startup is yet to report its FY26 financials. Between FY23 and FY25, its revenue grew more than 3.4X to Rs 111 crore in FY25 from Rs 32.5 crore in FY23, while losses widened nearly 4.7X to Rs 18.32 crore from Rs 3.91 crore during the same period.
 
The company competes in India’s burger QSR market with VC-backed homegrown chains such as Burger Singh and Biggies Burger, alongside regional players including Jumboking and The Burger Company, as well as cloud-kitchen player Burgerama, among several others.

title: VerSe Innovation unveils global AI content platform SparkStation for studios, brands and creators
summary:
VerSe Innovation, the parent company of Dailyhunt and Josh, has launched SparkStation, an AI-powered content production platform that brings different stages of video and advertising production into a single workflow. The company unveiled the platform at Film Expo 2026 as it looks to target filmmakers, production houses, brands, agencies, creators and influencers.
SparkStation covers the production process from ideation and scripting to storyboarding, casting, location and costume design, shot creation, music and dialogue generation, editing, captioning, rendering and ad creation.  The platform is designed to allow users to move between these stages without switching between multiple tools.
For filmmakers, SparkStation includes tools such as story builder, script coverage, casting, location design and shot creation. Users can also generate music and dialogue and edit and render the final output. 
Importantly, projects can be exported to professional editing software including Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro and DaVinci Resolve, allowing production teams to retain their existing post-production workflows.
The platform also addresses consistency, which remains a challenge with AI-generated video. Users can lock five elements, including a character’s face, expression, wardrobe, location and props, and carry them across multiple scenes. 
Spark Station uses a model-agnostic AI layer to assign different tasks to models suited to them. Video generation, character creation, camera movements, voice and language can therefore be handled by different models while remaining within the same interface.
For brands, e-commerce companies and agencies, the platform supports image, video, UGC and performance ad creation. It can generate product creatives at catalogue scale and produce multiple versions of campaigns for different platforms, languages and formats. SparkStation also supports localisation in more than 60 languages, including changes to lip movements, emotional delivery and local expressions.
For creators and influencers, the company is offering templates and studio-style production tools through a credits-based model. Studios and brands will have access to seat-based SaaS plans, while larger customers can opt for enterprise licensing and API access.
VerSe claims SparkStation can reduce the cost of producing a 60-second brand film from Rs 10-25 lakh to Rs 50,000-75,000. It also expects production timelines to fall from several weeks to around 24 hours. These figures are company estimates and will need to be tested as the platform scales.

title: Aakash revenue stays flat at Rs 2,041 Cr in FY26; EBITDA plunges 65%
summary:
Aakash Educational Services (AESL) continued to deliver strong academic results in FY26, with its students securing nine ranks in the JEE Advanced 2026 Top 100 and 41 ranks in the NEET Top 100. However, this performance did not translate into meaningful financial growth as the test-prep company’s operating revenue remained largely flat, while its EBITDA plunged 65% during the last fiscal year.
Aakash’s revenue from operations stood at Rs 2,041 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 2,032 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Aakash derives almost all of its operating revenue from its coaching business, which includes classroom programmes run through its own centres. The segment contributed Rs 1,956 crore in FY26, largely unchanged from Rs 1,951 crore in the previous fiscal and accounted for around 96% of the company’s operating revenue.
The remaining revenue came from its franchisee network, where partner-run centres operate under the Aakash brand. Revenue from this segment rose 3.7% to Rs 84 crore in FY26 from Rs 81 crore a year earlier.
The company’s total income grew 3.3% to Rs 2,154 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,085 crore in FY25, aided by a more than twofold increase in other income to Rs 113 crore.
Employee benefit expenses, Aakash’s largest cost head, declined 2.4% to Rs 1,300 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,332 crore in FY25. Depreciation expenses fell 4.5% to Rs 235 crore, while advertising costs dropped 7% to Rs 146 crore.
Meanwhile, other expenses rose 6.5% to Rs 626 crore. This included costs related to security and housekeeping, subvention, legal and professional services, among other expenses. Franchise service fees also surged 66% to Rs 91 crore during the fiscal. Overall, the company's total expenses increased marginally to Rs 2,398 crore from Rs 2,378 crore in FY25.
Despite the marginal increase in revenue, its operating profitability weakened sharply. EBITDA fell 65% to Rs 15.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 43.3 crore in FY25, dragging its EBITDA margin to 0.75% from 2.13% in the previous fiscal. Its ROCE stood at -46.1% in FY26.
Overall, the firm narrowed its loss before tax and exceptional items by 17% year-on-year to Rs 244 crore in FY26 from Rs 293 crore in FY25.
The company reported a net loss of Rs 186.5 crore for the fiscal, with deferred tax adjustments and exceptional items having an impact on the reported figure. For a clearer view of its underlying operating performance, we have considered losses before tax and exceptional items in this analysis.
At the end of FY26, Aakash had total current assets of Rs 325 crore, including a cash and bank balance of Rs 112 crore.
The financial performance comes as Aakash remains at the centre of Byju’s ownership dispute. Byju’s acquired the test-prep chain for around $1 billion in 2021, while its stake has since been diluted, with Manipal Health emerging as the largest shareholder. As part of a proposed settlement, Byju’s lenders are in talks to acquire around 30% of Aakash at a valuation of nearly $2 billion.

Hero MotoCorp has increased its stake in electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy to around 32.8% by acquiring shares from GIC, the sovereign wealth fund of Singapore.
As per bulk deal data, Hero MotoCorp acquired 1.19 crore Ather shares from Government of Singapore (GIC) at Rs 1,480 apiece on August 28 on NSE, valuing the transaction at around Rs 1,758.24 crore.
The acquisition will take Hero MotoCorp’s holding in Ather from 29.88% to 32.8% on a fully diluted basis.
Ather is already an associate company of Hero MotoCorp and operates in the electric two-wheeler and charging infrastructure space. The company reported a turnover of Rs 3,671.76 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 2,255 crore in FY25 and Rs 1,753.8 crore in FY24.
Hero MotoCorp said the acquisition does not require any governmental or regulatory approvals.
Ather Energy recently raised Rs 1,200 crore through a preferential issue, with Hero MotoCorp investing nearly Rs 960 crore and the India-Japan Fund (IJF) investing Rs 200 crore. Co-founders Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain also invested Rs 20 crore each. Hero MotoCorp has been steadily increasing its investment in Ather, with the latest transaction marking another such investment.
According to Vahan data, Ather Energy retained the third position with 28,819 registrations and a 14.89% market share in July. The company recorded an 8.3% month-on-month decline, with 2,616 fewer registrations than in June.
Following the latest deal, Ather’s shares closed 8% higher at Rs 1,616.3, taking its market capitalization to Rs 63,762 crore, or around $6.7 billion.

title: Furlenco nears Rs 400 Cr revenue in FY26, profit jumps 19X
summary:
Since Sheela Foam picked up a 35% stake in Furlenco, the furniture rental company’s revenue from operations has grown 2.6X in two years, rising from Rs 140 crore in FY24 to Rs 370 crore in FY26. Furlenco has also remained profitable, posting a profit of around Rs 60 crore in FY26.

The Bengaluru-based company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 370.43 crore in FY26 from Rs 228.74 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.


Furlenco provides furniture and home decor for rent along with relocation services. Income from furniture rental services accounted for 92% of the operating revneue which increased 64% to Rs 341.07 crore. While the sale sale of products grew 38% to Rs 29.36 crore in the said period.
Furlenco also reported Rs 4.99 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 375.42 crore in FY26 from Rs 240.05 crore in FY25.
On the cost front, depreciation and finance costs rose sharply by 57.5% and 75.6%, respectively. Employee expenses increased 17.1% to Rs 36.18 crore, while material costs nearly 3X jumped to Rs 27.01 crore during the previous fiscal year ended March 2026.
The company did not provide a detailed breakup of other expenses, which rose 34.4% to Rs 181.04 crore in FY26 from Rs 134.7 crore in FY25. The financial statements classify these expenses as miscellaneous expenses.  Overall, Furlenco’s total expenses grew 45.1% to Rs 343.85 crore in FY26 from Rs 236.94 crore in FY25.
With revenue growth outpacing the rise in expenses, Furlenco’s profit surged 19.1X to Rs 59.52 crore in FY26 from Rs 3.11 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA also nearly doubled to Rs 129.5 crore, pushing the EBITDA margin to 35.01%. Meanwhile, ROCE improved to 13.17% from 5.37%.


On a unit basis, Furlenco spent Rs 0.93 to earn every rupee of operating revenue, improving from Rs 1.03 in FY25. Its cash and bank balances more than doubled to Rs 75 crore from Rs 32 crore, while total current assets increased 67.9% to Rs 178 crore in FY26.

Furlenco competes with Rentomojo in the furniture and home appliance rental market. Rentomojo recently received SEBI’s observations for its proposed IPO, which comprises a Rs 150 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale of up to 28.4 million shares. The company reported Rs 265.96 crore in revenue and Rs 43.11 crore in profit in FY25.

title: PRISM’s FY26 profit jumps 4X to Rs 994 Cr, revenue jumps 50%
summary:
OYO’s parent company PRISM reported a sharp improvement in profitability in FY26, with profit after tax (PAT) jumping over four-fold to Rs 994 crore from Rs 245 crore in FY25, while revenue grew nearly 50% year-on-year.
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 9,358 crore from Rs 6,353 crore in FY25, according to its annual report accessed by Entrackr.

PRISM’s EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 2,594 crore during the fiscal year. However, the bottom line included a deferred tax credit of Rs 678 crore. The company also incurred Rs 1,414 crore in interest expenses during FY26.
PRISM’s gross booking value (GBV) surged 88.5% YoY to Rs 30,683 crore, led by higher business volumes, premium and company-serviced hotels, and the full-year contribution from G6 Hospitality, PRISM’s American motel company.
G6 Hospitality contributed Rs 14,107 crore to the GBV in FY26, compared with Rs 3,529 crore in FY25. Excluding G6, hotel GBV grew 36.5% to Rs 10,939 crore, while the homes business grew 19.4% to Rs 5,447 crore.
North America emerged as a key growth driver after G6 made its first full-year contribution following its acquisition in December 2024. PRISM said it integrated G6’s technology stack into its unified platform within a year and deployed AI-led pricing and service tools across its properties.
Around 67% of room nights in FY26 came through non-commissionable channels, supported by the OYO app and other direct channels. The company launched its premium-focused CheckIn app in September 2025 to strengthen direct customer engagement and drive repeat demand.
PRISM continued to operate across more than 35 countries through a centralised technology and operating platform built largely from India. The company said the model helped it scale international operations while improving operating leverage.
Meanwhile, PRISM is progressing towards a proposed public listing and has filed an Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus-I (UDRHP-I) for a fresh issue of up to Rs 6,650 crore.

summary:
OORJAA, a technology-led logistics platform, has raised Rs 9.7 crore ($1 million) in a Series A funding round led by Equentis Angel Fund, with participation from Inflection Point Ventures (IPV). This is the first close of a larger round, for which the company is in advanced discussions with a few VC funds.
The fresh funds will be used for technology and product development, scaling Datashastra, its proprietary AI/SaaS logistics stack, and strengthening its control-tower and automation capabilities, OORJAA said in a press release.
The Mumbai-based startup had earlier secured $1.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Micello Fund, with participation from Capital-A, Java Capital, Anicut Capital and Lead Angels in September 2023. In October 2023, it raised Rs 5.35 crore in a pre-Series A 2 round from Inflection Point Ventures (IPV), Vinners Platform, Soonicorn Ventures and HEM Angels.
Co-founded in 2019 by Sandeep Patil, Prashant Mohite, Yogesh Parab and Umesh Singh, OORJAA is a technology-led logistics company operating mid-mile and last-mile networks across more than 200 Indian cities.
OORJAA’s proprietary AI stack, Datashastra, powers route optimisation, reconciliation and 24×7 control-tower visibility. The platform is also offered as a standalone SaaS suite internationally. Its differentiator is an outcome-linked cost-per-unit model, under which clients pay for units moved rather than assets deployed.
According to market research, the global logistics market is valued at $10 trillion, while the logistics SaaS segment, which Datashastra focuses on, is growing at a high single-digit to double-digit CAGR.
OORJAA claims to move more than 3 million products and 50,000 last-mile orders daily across over 200 cities, while maintaining 95% SLA compliance for enterprise clients including Zepto, Blinkit, Amazon and Swiggy. The company is also deploying EVs across dense urban clusters to further lower unit costs and emissions.
Technology-led logistics platforms are becoming an increasingly important part of India’s startup ecosystem, using AI, SaaS, automation, real-time tracking, data analytics and digital marketplaces to address inefficiencies in the country’s fragmented freight and supply-chain sector.

title: Temple acquires London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous
summary:
Deepinder Goyal-led healthtech startup Temple has acquired London-based Longevous, an evidence-based longevity medicine practice, as it looks to strengthen its clinical and scientific capabilities ahead of its launch.
The acquisition will bring Longevous founders Dr Robert Mohr and Dr Avi Roy, along with their team, into Temple full time, Goyal said in a post on X.
Dr Mohr will join Temple as Chief Medical Officer. A board-certified physician with nearly two decades of clinical experience, Mohr moved from emergency medicine to longevity medicine, with expertise spanning preventive and precision medicine.
Meanwhile, Roy will join Temple as Head of Science. An Oxford-trained biomedical scientist, Roy has worked at the intersection of longevity science and business. He is the co-founder of Founders Health and UDA and was previously a research fellow at the Centre for the Advancement of Sustainable Medical Innovation at the University of Oxford.
According to Goyal, the duo first met him at a dinner event in London a couple of months ago. Their conversation around longevity science eventually led them to try Temple themselves.
For the next two months, Mohr and Roy used Temple as their daily wearable and worked with its science team to evaluate its proprietary ‘Entropy’ metric and the data collected by the device. They also challenged some of the company’s assumptions and reviewed Temple’s first scientific manuscripts before submission.
“Given how personally invested they’d become, I asked if they’d consider building Temple with me full time,” Goyal said.
Longevous will continue to operate under Temple, with Mohr and Roy continuing to look after its existing clients.
Temple is Goyal’s healthtech venture focused on building wearable technology for tracking physiological signals and longevity-related metrics. The startup has been developing a wearable device that sits near the temple and has introduced a proprietary metric called Entropy, which it says measures the body’s real-time energy expenditure.

title: Exclusive: Even Healthcare lays off 350 employees
summary:
Healthtech startup Even Healthcare has raised back-to-back funding rounds this year, but the fresh capital has not stopped the company from laying off around 350 employees as it phases down its insurance business and shifts its focus to a hospital-led healthcare model.
Even Healthcare has laid off nearly 30–35% of its workforce, or around 350 employees, according to four sources familiar with the matter.
“The job cuts have impacted multiple teams and come as Even looks to reduce its cost base. The company is also restructuring parts of its business as it shifts resources towards its hospital-led healthcare model,” said one of the sources requesting anonymity.
The layoffs come at a difficult time for the Bengaluru-based startup, which is in the process of raising $50 million in a round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures. It has already raised $21 million in the first tranche, with the remaining amount expected to come in a subsequent tranche. Entrackr exclusively reported the funding round and its breakup on Wednesday.
“Sources said the restructuring is aimed at bringing down costs and improving operational efficiency,” said the person cited above.
According to sources, Even has been moving deeper into healthcare delivery after starting with a subscription-led model. The firm launched its first hospital in Bengaluru and is looking to expand its hospital network.
However, the expansion has come with a high cash burn. Even’s revenue from ops rose to Rs 27.2 crore in FY25 from Rs 8.3 crore in FY24, while its losses widened to Rs 90.2 crore from Rs 72.4 crore in the same period.
The company had raised $20 million in January 2026 from Lachy Groom and Alpha Wave Global. This followed a $30 million funding round in 2024, taking the total capital raised by Even to more than $70 million.
The proposed $50 million round, therefore, comes just months after its previous fundraise. The latest layoffs suggest that the company is now looking to tighten spending while it prepares for its next capital infusion.
Even’s latest restructuring points to the challenges of building a capital-intensive healthcare delivery business while managing the economics of its earlier model. As the firm reshapes its operations, the key question will be whether the new approach can improve unit economics and create a more sustainable path to growth. The outcome will also determine how effectively Even can translate fresh investor backing into a business that requires less capital to support each stage of its expansion.

title: VAHDAM India reports Rs 350 Cr revenue in FY26; profit jumps 6X
summary:
After turning profitable in FY25, direct-to-consumer (D2C) wellness brand VAHDAM India further strengthened its bottom line in FY26, with net profit zooming over sixfold to Rs 32 crore. The company continued to derive almost all of its revenue from international markets, with the US remaining its key market.
VAHDAM India's revenue from operations grew by 31% year-on-year to Rs 349.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 267.5 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statement filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

VAHDAM, a global wellness brand, offering herbal infusions & supplements, sources its products directly from farms across India and sells them in India and key global markets, including the US, Canada and Europe. Sales of these products remained the company’s primary revenue stream during the fiscal year.
International markets continued to account for the bulk of VAHDAM’s revenue, contributing nearly 96% of its total operating revenue at Rs 335.3 crore. The company also earned Rs 10.2 crore in non-operating income, taking its total revenue to Rs 359.8 crore in FY26.
For the D2C firm, advertising and promotional expenses emerged as its largest cost at Rs 95.9 crore which rose 65% year-on-year. Transportation was the second-largest expense at Rs 70 crore.
Cost of materials rose 32% year-on-year to Rs 63.4 crore, while employee expenses increased 30% to Rs 35 crore, including Rs 3.76 crore in ESOP expenses. The company also paid Rs 28.9 crore in commissions to selling agents. Other overheads, including rent, legal and professional fees and miscellaneous expenses, added Rs 41.4 crore, taking total costs to Rs 334.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 268.2 crore in FY25.
Coming to the bottom line, the company’s profit jumped over sixfold to Rs 32.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 5.2 crore in FY25, led by growth in its overseas revenue.

Its ROCE and EBITDA margin also improved to 9.5% and 5%, respectively, while EBITDA surged 2.7 times to Rs 17.5 crore during the period. On a unit level, the firm spent Rs 0.96 to earn a single rupee of operating revenue in FY26.
At the end  of March 2026, VAHDAM India reported Rs 154 crore of current assets including Rs 42 crore of cash and bank balance.
VAHDAM India has raised over $40 million in funding to date, including a recent $3 million round led by SIDBI Venture last year. Its lead investors include Fireside Ventures, Sixth Sense Ventures, and IIFL Asset Management.

title: A91, Sixth Sense-backed Pushp Brand gets SEBI nod for IPO
summary:
Packaged spices maker Pushp Brand (India) has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
According to the DRHP, the IPO will comprise an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 74.45 lakh equity shares by existing shareholders. The selling shareholders include promoters Surendra Kumar Surana and Mahendra Kumar Surana, along with investors A91 Emerging Fund I LLP and Sixth Sense India Opportunities III.
A91, which invested around Rs 125 crore in Pushp Brand in 2020, currently holds a 20.14% stake in the company. The investor will sell only a part of its holding through the OFS. Sixth Sense, which invested around Rs 101 crore in 2023, owns a 7.81% stake and will also partially exit through the IPO.
The company also appointed ICICI Securities, IIFL Capital Services and Systematix Corporate Services as the book running lead managers to the issue.
Founded in 1974 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, Pushp Brand has grown from a regional spices business into a packaged food company operating under the Pushp and Munimji brands. Its portfolio includes pure and blended spices, hing, whole spices and other products such as western seasonings, quick-fry mixes, soya products and tea.
As of March 2026, Pushp had 312 SKUs and a distribution network covering 24 states and union territories. Its products were sold through 1,016 distributors and more than 3.68 lakh retail touchpoints.
Financially, Pushp's revenue from operations rose 19% to Rs 482 crore in FY26 from Rs 405 crore in FY25 while its restated profit increased to Rs 58.95 crore from Rs 45.85 crore during the same period.
The company competes with established packaged spices brands such as Everest Food Products, Mahashian Di Hatti, Orkla India, Aachi Masala Foods, and Sakthi Masala, among others.
